nodes.name: pH-induced electrodeposition of Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH
nodes.procedure: The partially hydroxylated composite of Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH was synthesized through a facile pH-induced electrodeposition process using nickel source, sulfur source, and 7 mmol NH₄Cl. The pH control at the electrified electrode-electrolyte interface was achieved through the hydrolysis of NH₄Cl, which triggered formation of Ni₃S₂ and facilitated transformation of Ni(OH)₂ into Ni-OH. Optimal electrodeposition time was 700 s.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show disappearance of Ni(OH)₂ peaks and appearance of metallic nickel peaks (JCPDS No. 70-1849) for Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After introducing 7 mmol of NH₄Cl, peaks for Ni(OH)₂ in XRD patterns disappear, and new peaks for metallic nickel (JCPDS No. 70-1849) are observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectrum shows Ni₃S₂ characteristic peaks at ≈190, 209, 294, and 338 cm⁻¹ and broad peak at 516 cm⁻¹ indexed to hydroxyl species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of Ni₃S₂ is evidenced by the Raman spectrum, with characteristic peaks located at ≈190, 209, 294, and 338 cm⁻¹. Moreover, the broad peak around 516 cm⁻¹ is indexed to hydroxyl species.

nodes.characterization_summary: TG-MS shows hydroxyl content of 8.1 wt% for Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH, 7.5 wt% for Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH-3, and 19.1 wt% for Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The hydroxyl content is 8.1% for Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH, 7.5% for Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH-3, and 19.1% for Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM images display network of aggregated nanoparticles with flocculent surface for Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FESEM images of Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH (Figure 1D,E) displayed a network of aggregated nanoparticles with a flocculent surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals aggregated nanoparticles with layer of flocculent nanosheets covering the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images of Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH (Figure S5A,B, Supporting Information) also revealed aggregated nanoparticles, with a layer of flocculent nanosheets covering the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringe of 0.29 nm for Ni₃S₂ (110) plane and 0.21 nm for metallic Ni (111) plane at the interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM analysis (Figure 1F-H) provided detailed insights into the interfacial structure, revealing lattice fringes corresponding to Ni₃S₂ and metallic nickel. Specifically, the lattice fringe of 0.29 nm (the yellow tetragon) corresponds to the (110) plane of Ni₃S₂ and the lattice fringe of 0.21 nm (the orange tetragon) matches the (111) plane of metallic nickel.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms coexistence of Ni₃S₂ and metallic nickel.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH (Figure 1I) further confirms the coexistence of Ni₃S₂ and metallic nickel.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS and element mappings indicate O, S, and Ni are uniformly distributed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The relevant energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy and element mappings (Figures S5C,D, Supporting Information) indicate that O, S, and Ni are uniformly distributed.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s peaks at 531.2 eV (hydroxyl) and 532.4 eV (adsorbed H₂O); Ni 2p peaks at 853.0 eV (metallic Ni) and 855.8 eV (Ni₃S₂); S 2p peaks at 162.6 and 164.1 eV (Ni-S); higher proportion of hydroxyl species than Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH-3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution O 1s spectrum of Ni₃S₂/Ni OH reveals the peaks at 531.2 and 532.4 eV, indexed to the hydroxyl species and adsorbed H₂O... the binding energies of nickel species for metallic nickel and Ni₃S₂ are determined to be 853.0 and 855.8 eV in Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH... the S 2p XPS spectra provide evidence for the presence of Ni-S species in Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH, with peaks centered at 162.6 and 164.1 eV... Notably, the proportion of hydroxyl species in Ni₃S₂/Ni OH is higher than that in Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH-3.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES curves analogous to nickel foil, higher absorption edge for Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH indicating higher Ni oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH, Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH-3, and nickel foil exhibited analogous XANES curves... the sample of Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH manifests a higher absorption edge, compared with the Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH-3 and nickel foil.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows Ni-Ni, Ni-O, and Ni-S bonds at ≈2.52, 2.23, and 2.26 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EXAFS spectra (Figure 2E) and Fourier transform κ³-weighted oscillation curves (Figure S10, Supporting Information) showed the Ni-Ni, Ni-O, and Ni-S bonds in the measured samples, with the peaks located at ≈2.52, 2.23, and 2.26 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: WT-EXAFS contour plots show Ni-O bonds but no Ni-Ni bonds characteristic of Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the contour plots of the Ni K-edge wavelet transform EXAFS (WT-EXAFS) distinctly illustrate that Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH and Ni₃S₂/Ni-OH-3 exhibited Ni-O bonds (the yellow line) but no Ni-Ni bonds (the red line) of the Ni(OH)₂.
